The timing and step cap are fixed in clearly named constants.

terms.meaning: Showing recorded work again over time, as though it were happening.
A group of recorded entries revealed together in one step.
A browser setting that asks websites to reduce animation.

sections.name: File setup, Step
sections.title: Setup and timing
sections.what: Imports React hooks, icons, the stage type, the work-line helper and the duration formatter, and sets the cap of 12 batches per stage and 700 milliseconds per step.
sections.why: These two numbers set how fast and how finely playback moves.
sections.watch_out: Changing the step time changes the pace of every replay.

sections.name: reducedMotion
sections.title: Reduced motion check
sections.what: Checks whether the visitor has asked the browser to reduce motion.
sections.why: Respects accessibility settings by starting playback paused.
sections.watch_out: Without a browser window the check returns false, so it is only meaningful in the browser.

sections.name: useRecordedPlayback, Playback
sections.title: Replay steps and controls
sections.what: Builds the steps, moves through them on a timer, marks each stage as running, complete or pending for the current moment, and returns play, pause, step, skip and the recorded duration.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a recorded run be watched through the same stage view as a live run, using its own recorded timing.
sections.watch_out: Pressing play after finishing restarts from the first step, but the results flag stays set, so results remain visible during the replay.

sections.name: PlaybackControls
sections.title: Playback progress and control buttons
sections.what: Shows a replay bar with a percentage, a short note that the replay uses saved records and runs nothing new, and buttons to pause, play, resume, replay, step forward or jump to the results. The buttons turn off when the replay has finished.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The on-screen note makes clear that replay is a recording and does not run any work.
sections.watch_out: The percentage is shown as 100 when the total is zero, so an empty replay looks complete.

summary: Replays a finished run's saved stage records step by step, so a run that already happened appears to unfold, without generating anything new.
purpose: Lets a visitor watch a recorded run as the live view would show it, with play, pause, step and skip controls.
why: The code comment says the pace is only a playback speed for recorded work and must never suggest the run is happening now.
how: Builds a list of steps for each stage: a start, a set of batches that reveal more of the stage's recorded entries, and a finished step. A timer moves through the steps at a fixed interval. Earlier stages show as complete, the current one as running with its recorded outcome noted, and later ones as pending. When the last step is reached, playing stops and results are shown. Users who prefer reduced motion start paused.
inputs: The list of stage records for the run, with their entries read through `workEvents`, and the browser's reduced-motion setting.
outputs: An adjusted stage list for the live track view, a flag for when results are shown, the recorded duration, and the control functions.
risks: Each stage is capped at 12 batches, so a stage with many entries reveals in large jumps. The timer restarts on every step.
debug: If playback freezes, check the cursor value and whether finished is true. If results never appear, check that the last step exists. If the duration is blank, check that stages have start and finish times. If playback starts paused, check the reduced-motion browser setting.
